relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with a clinical diagnosis of arterial tortuosity syndrome ("discovered incidentally to have ATS at the age of 5 days"); no SLC2A10 variant or genetic testing is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no script transcribed a table (Table 1 is flow/distensibility measurements for the single patient). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No variants table rows: the paper reports no SLC2A10 variant and no genetic testing, so the diagnosis appears clinical/imaging-based. n_patients_reported left null because the field counts patients with a SLC2A10 variant and none is reported. The two adult patients previously reported by the authors' group (ref ^8, Tsang 2007; Figure 4) were given no rows: the paper says only that 'In retrospect, these patient share the same features of ATS', which is a retrospective resemblance rather than a diagnosis, and their features are described jointly; cites_prior_report_of_same_patients was set true and the citation recorded because the paper shows these previously reported patients (rule 7). First author: the header prints 'Kindi Hamood NAl' (apparently a mangled name order); value recorded as the first token 'Kindi' as printed. Ascending and proximal descending aortic aneurysms were not mapped to the checklist item 'aortic root aneurysm' (the paper does not mention the root). 'Stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches' recorded observed from 'the area that appeared narrowed in the aortic arch' with an 8.5 mmHg gradient; wording is somewhat hedged ('appeared'). Normal findings handled per D-27: 'did not have any dysmorphic features' and 'The rest of the clinical examination was unremarkable' were not used to exclude any specific checklist item (e.g. down-slanting palpebral fissures); the dysmorphic-features absence is recorded as stated. Bisoprolol/captopril were given 'for blood pressure control' but hypertension is not stated, so systemic hypertension is not reported. 'no arterial dissections have been reported in ATS' is a general literature statement, not about this patient. Possible tension (not treated as a contradiction): exam states 'no significant blood pressure difference between the upper and lower limbs', while Results cite a clinically measured difference of 10 mmHg; recorded as excluded 'significant' difference with the 10 mmHg value as detail. Age at diagnosis 5 days (ATS discovered at that age); age at last evaluation 3 years; age at onset not stated.
